standard.description: This standard specifies standard guidelines, parameters, data requirements, and layout criteria for planning and designing river powerhouses integrated with barrages (barrage powerhouses) to optimize water utilization, determine power-generation layouts, and establish geotechnical and hydrological design boundaries.

certification.description: Voluntary Code of Practice. Since IS 14592 (Part 1) : 1998 is an engineering guideline for civil and electro-mechanical planning rather than a physical consumer product, it does not carry an individual mandatory BIS 'ISI Mark' product stamp. However, compliance with its site-investigation steps, soil boring counts, and water scheduling is strictly mandated in public sector tenders for run-of-the-river or low-head hydro projects (under CWC, NHPC, SJVN, state power corporations, and irrigation departments) to obtain technical clearance and validate Detailed Project Reports (DPRs). Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Requires compiling and evaluating information regarding the high flood level (HFL) using physical flood marks and local field enquiries to define safety elevations against powerhouse flooding.
Mandates collecting detailed data on 10-daily irrigation withdrawals at the proposed barrage, if any, to coordinate power generation schedules with agriculture diversion demands.

Requires establishing a gauge (stage) and discharge relation curve extending up to the design flood level, based on historical field data covering at least five (5) years, but preferably supported by observations and acceptable extrapolation.

Requires compiling daily rainfall data from all rainfall gauging stations situated within and around the local catchment area, covering as many years of historical record as possible to support design flood estimations.

Any observed or calculated test or analysis value (such as river stages, discharge rates, rainfall counts, or geological coordinates) must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960. The number of significant places retained must be identical to the specified value in the standard.
